claim: Under-30 visitors can buy a 2nd Sector Stalls U30 ticket for €30, excluding premieres, opening nights and Saturdays.
quote: If you are under 30, thanks to the U Are Invited project organised by Fondazione Arena and UniCredit, you can access 2nd Sector Stalls U30 for just €30. ... Première performances on 12 and 13 June, opening nights and Saturday performances are excluded.

claim: Unnumbered stone steps (gradinata) run roughly €20-30, numbered gradinata €40-75, and premium central parterre €180-250 for 2026.
quote: unreserved stone steps (gradinata) €20-30 ... numbered gradinata €40-75 ... premium central parterre €180-250 ... Opera performances range €20-250 depending on seating section

claim: Unnumbered first-come stone seats cost €25-40 and numbered arena-floor poltronissima seats €120-250 for the 2026 festival.
quote: Stone seats (unnumbered, first-come-first-served): €25-40. ... Numbered seats on the arena floor (poltronissima): €120-250. ... Opera festival tickets (summer evenings, mid-June to mid-September): €25-250 depending on seating.

claim: Premiere/opening-night performances command premiums, with packaged premiere-night Poltronissima Gold seats listed from €425 up to €455.
quote: €425 (listed for multiple individual opera performances: LA TRAVIATA, AIDA, NABUCCO, LA BOHÈME) ... €455 (higher price tier for some performances like LA TRAVIATA on June 27)

claim: Reduced Poltrone tickets are restricted to under-30 or over-65 visitors, and the seating hierarchy runs Poltronissima Platinum/Gold/Silver/Standard down to Poltrone, Verdi Sector and unnumbered gradinata.
quote: Tickets marked as Poltrone (reduced) are only available for visitors under 30 years old or over 65 years old. ... Poltronissime Platinum, Gold, Silver, and Standard ... Poltrone ... Verdi Sector ... Gradinata (unnumbered stone steps)
